nodes.label: Agents' Last Exam (ALE): Benchmark for Economically Valuable Tasks
nodes.author: Yiyou Sun et al.
nodes.rationale: ALE is a benchmark of 1K+ task instances spanning 55 subfields and 13 industry clusters, designed to evaluate AI agents on long-horizon, economically valuable, real-world tasks with verifiable outcomes.

nodes.label: Generalist Computer-Use Agent (GCUA)
nodes.author: Yiyou Sun et al.
nodes.rationale: GCUA is an agent with full capability across five functional layers: Brain (LLM reasoning), Eyes (GUI perception), Body (orchestration), Hands (tool invocation), and Feet (runtime substrate).

nodes.label: GUI-as-Tool: Desktop Action Integration
nodes.author: Yiyou Sun et al.
nodes.rationale: GUI-as-Tool exposes 14 desktop-action tools (keyboard, mouse, screenshot, utility) as standard entries in the agent's tool system via MCP bridge.

nodes.label: ALE-CLI: Linux-Only CLI-Focused Sub-Benchmark
nodes.author: Yiyou Sun et al.
nodes.rationale: ALE-CLI is a 105-task subset of ALE containing only Linux terminal-centric tasks; it enables comparison with CLI-only agents while maintaining harder difficulty than Terminal-Bench.

nodes.label: ALE-Claw: Self-Implemented GCUA Reference
nodes.author: Yiyou Sun et al.
nodes.rationale: ALE-Claw is a simplified Python implementation derived from OpenClaw that tests whether basic GCUA components suffice for comparable performance to frontier harnesses.

nodes.label: SOC 2018 / O*NET Occupational Taxonomy
nodes.author: Yiyou Sun et al.
nodes.rationale: ALE grounds its taxonomy in SOC 2018 and O*NET to ensure broad and representative industry coverage; 55 subdomains grouped into 13 domains.

nodes.label: ALE Evaluation Modes: Deterministic Scoring
nodes.author: Yiyou Sun et al.
nodes.rationale: ALE deliberately avoids LLM-as-judge wherever deterministic alternatives exist; 93.2% of tasks use code-based judges, with LLM judging reserved for creative/perceptual deliverables using narrow yes/no probes.

nodes.label: Gate-and-Score Pattern: Hard Precondition + Continuous Score
nodes.author: Yiyou Sun et al.
nodes.rationale: Gate-and-score prevents reward hacking by forcing 0 on hard precondition failure before any quality metric is evaluated; most common composition pattern in ALE.

nodes.label: ALE Difficulty Tiers: Near-Term, Full-Spectrum, Last-Exam
nodes.author: Yiyou Sun et al.
nodes.rationale: Three tiers allow community to choose evaluation budget: Near-Term (67 tasks, ~40% pass rate), Full-Spectrum (55 tasks, one per subdomain), Last-Exam (38 tasks, hardest, mostly 0% pass rate).

nodes.label: Codex: OpenAI Software Engineering Agent
nodes.author: Yiyou Sun et al.
nodes.rationale: Codex with GPT-5.5 achieves 24.0% overall pass rate on ALE, the strongest mainstream harness configuration; 82% on Terminal-Bench but only 23.3% on ALE-CLI.

nodes.label: Claude Code: Anthropic Agentic Coding Tool
nodes.author: Yiyou Sun et al.
nodes.rationale: Claude Code with Fable 5 achieves 22.0% overall pass rate on ALE; demonstrates that product-grade agents still struggle with economically valuable long-horizon tasks.

nodes.label: OpenClaw: Open-Source Agent Runtime
nodes.author: Yiyou Sun et al.
nodes.rationale: OpenClaw is used as baseline harness for model comparisons; ALE-Claw is a Python port of OpenClaw's agent loop with GUI-as-Tool additions.

nodes.label: ALE Failure Taxonomy: Understanding, Approach, Execution, Infrastructure
nodes.author: Yiyou Sun et al.
nodes.rationale: Two-level failure taxonomy shows Understanding and Approach failures (domain knowledge gaps, wrong strategy) account for ~75% of failures; dominant bottleneck is domain knowledge not execution.
